stories.title: Swiss tourist sentenced to prison after violating ‘Day of Silence’ in Bali
stories.summary: A Swiss tourist was sentenced to one year in prison in Bali for disrespecting the sacred Hindu Day of Silence (Nyepi) by posting provocative videos on Instagram. The tourist ignored local rules requiring silence and staying indoors, angered by restrictions, and his posts sparked widespread criticism from Balinese residents. He was arrested after apologising to an Indonesian senator, charged with religious hate speech, highlighting strict enforcement of local customs during Nyepi. A Swiss tourist is serving a yearlong sentence on the Indonesian resort island of Bali after prosecutors say he violated a sacred Hindu ritual and insulted it on Instagram. Luzian Andrin Zgraggen, 26, a construction worker from Switzerland, was found guilty of breaking Indonesian law by posting a provocative video to his Instagram story about the Day of Silence, known locally as Nyepi, on March 19. During this 24-hour period, locals and tourists alike are required to remain in their homes or hotels, keep lights dim and minimise noise, and are urged to perform quiet meditation. According to court documents, Zgraggen arrived in Bali on Feb 10 for vacation. Before the Day of Silence in March, hotel staff had explained the relevant restrictions. Prosecutors said Zgraggen became frustrated that he could not freely leave the hotel to find food and “displayed his anger” on social media, according to an online copy of his indictment. One video showed Zgraggen walking in the dark with a caption that said it was “pretty peaceful outside”, followed by an expletive about the rules around the religious holiday. After receiving thousands of negative comments, Zgraggen took down the posts. But the videos were screen-recorded and widely reposted to other popular accounts, drawing criticism from Balinese residents who found his actions disrespectful.
